question: What document clearly lists who is responsible for specific tasks and when they are due after a meeting?

options.A: A patient care plan
options.B: A hospital discharge summary
options.C: An annual financial budget
options.D: An action log

explanation: An action log tracks follow-up tasks with clear owners and deadlines so decisions actually get done. [learn more](GST321_U7_T4#GST321_U7_T4_h6)

question: In healthcare, what do we mean by 'information asymmetry'?

options.A: Pharmacies hide drug prices from the public
options.B: Government agencies control all hospital budgets
options.C: Patients and doctors share the exact same level of medical knowledge
options.D: Healthcare providers have deep medical training while patients know very little

explanation: You got it! It simply describes the knowledge gap: doctors and nurses spent years studying medicine, while patients usually rely on them to explain what is wrong. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h5)

question: How do cancer cells frequently manipulate apoptosis to survive and multiply?

options.A: They trigger excessive external death receptor signals
options.B: They replace damaged mitochondria with healthy ones
options.C: They mutate regulatory genes to evade programmed cell death
options.D: They speed up the intrinsic pathway to destroy healthy tissue

explanation: Cancer cells often survive by disabling the normal suicide signals that would normally force a damaged cell to die. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T5#GNS321_U1_T5_h7)

question: What tool should nurses tell parents to use for measuring liquid children's medicines at home?

options.A: A regular dining teaspoon
options.B: An open plastic drinking cup
options.C: A calibrated oral syringe
options.D: A standard kitchen soup spoon

explanation: Kitchen spoons come in all sizes and lead to wrong doses. Oral syringes give exact measurements every single time. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T6#GNS215_U6_T6_h8)

question: In which clinical situation would a doctor most likely use an intraarterial route?

options.A: Administering a routine morning dose of oral antibiotics
options.B: Providing daily maintenance fluids for a stable surgical patient
options.C: Giving an intramuscular vaccination for tetanus prevention
options.D: Delivering targeted chemotherapy directly to a liver tumor

explanation: Spot on! When doctors want to hit a specific trouble spot—like a tumor—with maximum medicine power without flooding the whole body, the intraarterial route is super useful. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T13#GNS125_U3_T13_h2)

question: How does hospital underfunding directly affect patient recovery outcomes?

options.A: It lowers the cost of prescription medications
options.B: It guarantees faster healing through natural immunity
options.C: It increases mortality rates and prolongs hospital stays
options.D: It prevents patients from contracting hospital infections

explanation: Lack of supplies, broken equipment, and overworked staff lead to delayed care and worse health outcomes for patients. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h5)

question: What is the main law protecting the rights of children in Nigeria?

options.A: The Adult Criminal Code
options.B: The Child Rights Act
options.C: The Public Land Decree
options.D: The National Health Insurance Act

explanation: Spot on! The Child Rights Act is the key legal framework safeguarding the welfare and special protection of minors in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h7)

question: What might patients do when health care costs become too high?

options.A: Patients usually demand extra diagnostic tests
options.B: Patients become less likely to ask questions about treatment
options.C: Patients may delay seeking care or skip needed medications
options.D: Patients tend to exercise more to stay out of the hospital

explanation: When medical bills get overwhelming, many people unfortunately try to save money by avoiding the clinic or cutting down their medication doses. [learn more](GST322_U2_T1#GST322_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why aren't standard antibody blood tests ideal for diagnosing an active case of onchocerciasis?

options.A: They only work during the first week of a bite
options.B: They require frozen tissue samples to function
options.C: They show past exposure rather than current infection
options.D: They cannot detect any immune response in humans

explanation: Antibodies stick around in the blood long after the body has dealt with the parasite. A positive blood test just means past exposure, not necessarily an active worm load right now. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T7#GNS214_U1_T7_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a good idea if you are facing backlash or resistance for your advocacy work?

options.A: Building strong community alliances
options.B: Relying strictly on verified factual data
options.C: Collaborating with professional nursing bodies
options.D: Acting completely alone without informing anyone

explanation: Correct! Trying to fight battles all by yourself puts you at high risk. True safety and strength always come from teamwork and professional support. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T14#GNS225_U2_T14_h8)

question: Into how many main categories does the World Health Organization divide FGM?

options.A: Six distinct types
options.B: Two distinct types
options.C: Four distinct types
options.D: Three distinct types

explanation: You got it! The WHO classifies FGM into four broad types based on the method and extent of tissue removed. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T2#GNS225_U6_T2_h2)

question: What major feature separates fungi and parasites from bacteria?

options.A: They possess viral capsids instead of cell walls
options.B: They can only survive without oxygen
options.C: They are eukaryotic with a true nucleus
options.D: They lack any form of genetic material

explanation: Unlike bacteria (which are simple prokaryotes), fungi and parasites are eukaryotes—meaning their cells have a proper, organized nucleus, just like human cells do. [learn more](GST114_U1_T4#GST114_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is usually the very first sign of leprosy on the skin?

options.A: A discolored patch that feels numb or less sensitive
options.B: Tiny water blisters on the hands
options.C: Painful open sores on the legs
options.D: Severe itching all over the body

explanation: A pale or reddish skin patch that doesn't feel normal touch or temperature is the classic early warning sign. Keep shining! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T6#GNS214_U1_T6_h4)

question: What does a nurse check when assessing normal uterine involution during a postnatal home visit?

options.A: The complete absence of lochia discharge after twenty-four hours
options.B: The permanent softening of the abdominal wall muscles
options.C: The gradual decrease in the size and height of the uterus
options.D: The rapid increase in maternal body weight

explanation: Involution is the normal process where the uterus returns to its pre-pregnancy size, felt as a steadily lowering fundal height. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h5)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?

options.A: Managing household financial accounts
options.B: Driving a car to the grocery store
options.C: Preparing a hot meal on the stove
options.D: Eating a meal independently

explanation: ADLs are the fundamental things we do every day to care for ourselves, like eating, bathing, dressing, and walking around. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h6)

question: Which type of poultice is commonly used to retain heat for deep inflammation and boils?

options.A: Kaolin poultice
options.B: Salt crystal poultice
options.C: Dry cotton poultice
options.D: Ice water poultice

explanation: Kaolin is a heavy clay substance known for holding heat well to treat deep-seated swelling and boils. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T10#GNS221_U3_T10_h3)

question: How does cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) help someone recovering from substance use?

options.A: By forcing them to forget all memories of their friends and family
options.B: By curing any physical infections caused by dirty needles
options.C: By helping them recognize personal triggers and build healthy coping mechanisms
options.D: By replacing their natural blood chemistry with artificial synthetic hormones

explanation: CBT is fantastic because it trains the mind to spot what triggers cravings and teaches healthier ways to handle life's stress. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T3#GNS125_U4_T3_h5)

question: Why do older adults frequently struggle with constipation?

options.A: Overactive muscular contractions in the stomach
options.B: Excessive production of digestive enzymes
options.C: Slower peristalsis and reduced intestinal motility
options.D: Rapid absorption of water in the upper bowel

explanation: Exactly! As the gut ages, its muscle contractions slow down. This gives the body more time to absorb water from waste, leading to hard, difficult stools. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h3)

question: A pregnant patient at 32 weeks comes in with bright red bleeding, and placenta previa is suspected. What action must the nurse NEVER do?

options.A: Performing a digital vaginal examination
options.B: Applying an electronic fetal monitor
options.C: Starting a large-bore intravenous line
options.D: Checking maternal blood pressure

explanation: Never put your fingers inside when placenta previa is suspected! Doing a digital exam can poke the placenta and trigger massive, life-threatening bleeding. Always check the ultrasound first. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h8)

question: A patient comes in with a warm, swollen, and painful knee after light activity. What is most likely going on?

options.A: Complete cessation of local osteoclast activity
options.B: Rapid mineralization of the surrounding bone matrix
options.C: Local inflammation and fluid accumulation in the joint
options.D: Immediate formation of a hard bony callus bridge

explanation: Warmth, swelling, and pain are classic signs of inflammation and fluid buildup inside the joint space. Great clinical deduction! [learn more](GNS222_U1_T20#GNS222_U1_T20_h6)

question: Which condition makes cervical traction completely unsafe (a contraindication)?

options.A: Unstable spinal fractures
options.B: Degenerative disc disease
options.C: Cervical radiculopathy
options.D: Mild muscle spasms

explanation: Spot on! Pulling on a broken, unstable spine can cause terrible damage to the spinal cord. Safety first! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T12#GNS221_U1_T12_h3)

question: Why do traditional health clinics often make teenage patients feel unwelcome?

options.A: They only open during late night hours when teenagers are in school
options.B: They are required by law to report all visits to local police stations
options.C: They completely lack basic medical equipment for younger populations
options.D: They are usually structured and designed primarily for adults or young children

explanation: Standard clinics often overlook the specific developmental, social, and emotional needs of teenagers, making them feel out of place. You've got this! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T18#GNS312_U3_T18_h1)

question: How should a nurse best approach a caregiver who expresses fear and hesitation about routine childhood vaccines?

options.A: Scold the parent for ignoring professional medical advice
options.B: Report the parent to local law enforcement authorities
options.C: Listen respectfully and provide clear, reassuring education
options.D: Ignore their concerns and administer the vaccines anyway

explanation: Building trust through empathetic listening and clear, respectful communication is the most effective way to address vaccine hesitancy and correct rumors. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h8)

question: What is the medical term for menstrual bleeding that is unusually heavy or lasts too long?

options.A: Metrorrhagia
options.B: Menorrhagia
options.C: Dysmenorrhea
options.D: Amenorrhea

explanation: Menorrhagia is the term for extra heavy or long periods. You will see this often in clinical practice when patients complain about soaking through pads too quickly. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T12#GNS311_U1_T12_h2)

question: Which phrase is an example of unhelpful communication when talking to a dying patient?

options.A: "It is okay to cry and feel upset right now."
options.B: "Everything is going to be completely fine."
options.C: "I am right here with you through this."
options.D: "Tell me more about what you are feeling today."

explanation: False reassurances dismiss the patient's real fears and isolate them from honest conversation. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h5)

question: What is the main difference between latent TB and active TB disease?

options.A: Latent TB bacteria are dead, while active TB bacteria are alive.
options.B: Latent TB requires hospital admission, while active TB is treated at home.
options.C: Latent TB only affects children, while active TB only affects adults.
options.D: Latent TB has no symptoms and is not contagious, whereas active TB causes illness and spreads.

explanation: Think of latent TB as sleeping quietly in the body—the person feels fine and cannot pass it on. Active TB is awake, causing illness, and can spread to others. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is considered an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?

options.A: Bathing and dressing
options.B: Balancing a checkbook
options.C: Shopping for groceries
options.D: Driving a motor vehicle

explanation: You nailed it! ADLs are the basic self-care tasks we do every day—like bathing, dressing, eating, and moving around. Simple and fundamental! [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h5)

question: Why do health problems after a disaster often last a very long time?

options.A: Because government funding stops immediately after impact
options.B: Because surviving community members always relocate permanently
options.C: Because fixing broken toilets, clean water systems, and clinics takes time
options.D: Because emergency relief teams refuse to leave the area

explanation: It takes months or even years to rebuild basic things like clean water and medical care. That's why health struggles continue long after the main event. Keep learning at your own pace! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T11#GNS315_U1_T11_h1)

question: Why is it so important to talk about family planning before discharging a post-abortion care patient?

options.A: Contraceptives cure existing pelvic infections
options.B: Hospital policy mandates permanent sterilization
options.C: It prevents the onset of menopausal symptoms
options.D: Fertility can return very quickly after a termination

explanation: Brilliant! Ovulation can start as early as two weeks after an abortion, so counseling helps prevent unplanned repeat pregnancies. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h6)

question: How do you know for sure if a patient truly understood your health education instructions?

options.A: Asking the patient to explain the instructions back in their own words
options.B: Ensuring the nurse spoke clearly without using medical jargon
options.C: Writing down all the medication dosages on a whiteboard
options.D: Handing the patient a printed pamphlet before leaving the room

explanation: This is the classic 'teach-back' method! Asking them to explain it in their own words helps you catch any confusion without making them feel small. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T23#GNS225_U2_T23_h2)

question: What is a simple, practical habit to ensure a patient gets a wide variety of helpful antioxidants and plant nutrients?

options.A: Eating a colorful variety of different fruits and vegetables every day
options.B: Eating the exact same single vegetable for every meal to track intake
options.C: Choosing only white and beige foods because they digest more easily
options.D: Relying entirely on multi-vitamin pills while avoiding fresh produce

explanation: Spot on! Different plant colors mean different health-boosting compounds, so eating a rainbow is always the best prescription. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h6)

question: If you want to attend a learning session focused strictly on practicing physical skills with supervision, which one should you pick?

options.A: A workshop
options.B: A conference
options.C: A lecture series
options.D: A seminar

explanation: Workshops are all about action! Instead of just sitting and listening, you get your hands dirty practicing procedures under the watchful eye of an expert. [learn more](GST321_U8_T8#GST321_U8_T8_h3)

question: Which baby health problems are most common when born to teenage mothers?

options.A: Congenital heart murmurs caused by maternal stress
options.B: Advanced bone maturation at birth
options.C: Premature birth and low birth weight
options.D: Excessive birth weight and overgrown organs

explanation: Spot on! Because the mother's body is still growing, babies often arrive too early and small. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T13#GNS312_U1_T13_h5)

question: What is evaluated during a functional assessment prior to admission?

options.A: Financial credit history
options.B: Workplace performance record
options.C: Previous travel experiences
options.D: Activities of daily living

explanation: A functional assessment looks closely at how well a potential resident can manage basic daily self-care tasks like bathing and dressing. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h2)

question: A patient develops scar tissue inside her uterus after a complicated D&C (dilation and curettage) procedure. What is this condition called?

options.A: Endometrial hyperplasia
options.B: Asherman's syndrome
options.C: Adenomyosis
options.D: Uterine didelphys

explanation: You nailed it! Asherman's syndrome refers to intrauterine adhesions or scars that typically form following surgeries inside the uterine cavity. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T19#GNS216_U5_T19_h2)

question: What term describes an infant's inborn, natural mood and emotional reactivity?

options.A: Psyche
options.B: Consciousness
options.C: Delusion
options.D: Temperament

explanation: Temperament refers to the biologically rooted behavioral and emotional traits that babies are born with. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T8#GNS314_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why must an emergency CT scan be done immediately for a suspected stroke patient?

options.A: To check for bacterial meningitis
options.B: To rule out intracranial hemorrhage
options.C: To calculate total intracranial blood volume
options.D: To measure electrical brain wave activity

explanation: Spot on! We need to check if the stroke is caused by bleeding. Giving clot-busting medications during a hemorrhagic stroke would be deadly. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h5)

question: What must you often handle first before trying to teach a patient about their discharge medications?

options.A: Discharge paperwork completion
options.B: Full payment of hospital bills
options.C: Severe pain or acute distress
options.D: Complete recovery of normal gait

explanation: If a patient is in terrible pain or panicking, their brain cannot focus on new instructions. Relief comes first, teaching comes second! [learn more](GST321_U8_T2#GST321_U8_T2_h5)

question: On day three of life, a newborn's face and chest look slightly yellow. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Neonatal tetanus infection
options.B: An acute allergic reaction to breastmilk
options.C: Normal physiological jaundice
options.D: Severe congenital heart disease

explanation: You're learning fast! Mild yellowing around day two or three is usually normal physiological jaundice as the baby's young liver processes extra red blood cells. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h5)

question: What should a nurse do if a patient consistently eats less than 30 percent of their food?

options.A: Wait two weeks to see if appetite returns on its own
options.B: Notify the dietitian and consider nutritional support options
options.C: Tell the patient that eating is mandatory for discharge
options.D: Remove all meal trays immediately without documenting intake

explanation: Poor intake puts patients at risk for malnutrition. Always team up with the dietitian early to help your patient get the nutrition they need! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h7)

question: Why do healthcare professionals use standardized anatomical terminology?

options.A: To replace traditional nursing assessment skills
options.B: To make medical records longer and more detailed
options.C: to confuse patients so they ask fewer questions
options.D: To prevent misunderstandings during clinical communication

explanation: Standardized terms give everyone a universal vocabulary so patient care details are never misunderstood across different shifts or teams. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T2#GNS111_U1_T2_h1)

question: A family caregiver is exhausted and needs a short break to run errands. Which hospice team member is best suited to sit with the patient during this time?

options.A: A medical social worker
options.B: A registered nurse
options.C: A hospice volunteer
options.D: A certified nursing assistant

explanation: Volunteers frequently provide companionship and respite care, giving family caregivers time away to rest or attend to personal errands. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T14#GNS324_U5_T14_h4)

question: Which position is best for an unconscious patient who is now breathing normally and has a pulse?

options.A: High Fowler position
options.B: Prone flat on the belly
options.C: Supine with legs raised
options.D: Recovery position

explanation: Roll them into the recovery position (on their side). This keeps their airway open and safe so they don't choke if they happen to vomit. [learn more](GNS315_U4_T3#GNS315_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is it super important to write down correct phone numbers and addresses during contact tracing?

options.A: To build a database for future academic research publications
options.B: To bill the contacts for public health screening services
options.C: To report community members who break curfew rules
options.D: To ensure tracers can quickly reach and monitor exposed persons

explanation: Makes total sense, right? Without the right phone number or address, our team cannot reach out to check on them or warn them if they start feeling unwell. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h2)

question: When would a researcher prefer to use 'incidence density' instead of cumulative incidence?

options.A: When every single person stays in the study until the end
options.B: When calculating the prevalence of a permanent birth defect
options.C: When study participants enter at different times or drop out
options.D: When the researcher only cares about counting total deaths

explanation: Incidence density uses person-time, which is a lifesaver when people join a study at different times or drop out along the way. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T11#GNS313_U1_T11_h4)

question: A newborn delivered after a tough, instrument-assisted birth is very sleepy (lethargic) and has a high-pitched cry. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Physiological moulding
options.B: Normal post-birth fatigue
options.C: Mild caput succedaneum
options.D: Intracranial hemorrhage

explanation: You nailed it. Unusual sleepiness and a high-pitched cry are classic red flags that there might be pressure or bleeding inside the baby's head. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T15#GNS121_U6_T15_h4)

question: What does the term 'nutrient density' mean?

options.A: Providing many vitamins and minerals relative to the calorie count
options.B: Being imported from foreign countries to ensure high quality
options.C: Containing only fats and proteins with zero carbohydrates
options.D: Having high amounts of calories and sugar in a small serving

explanation: Spot on! Nutrient-dense foods pack a heavy punch of vitamins and minerals into every single calorie, giving you the best value for your health. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h2)

question: Where should used razor blades from a delivery kit be placed immediately after use?

options.A: In a puncture-proof sharp container
options.B: In the general household trash bin
options.C: Underneath the plastic delivery sheet
options.D: Inside the clean cloth wrap for the baby

explanation: Sharps must be contained in rigid, puncture-proof containers to prevent accidental cuts and potential pathogen transmission. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h7)

question: When should a nurse use soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

options.A: When the clinic runs out of clean disposable gloves
options.B: Only at the very beginning of the morning shift
options.C: Before opening every single new vaccine vial
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Soap and water are required to physically wash away visible dirt, grime, and certain types of spores that alcohol rubs cannot clear effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T67#GNS214_U1_T67_h2)

question: Which blood protein acts like a sponge to hold fluid inside the blood vessels?

options.A: Globulin
options.B: Hemoglobin
options.C: Albumin
options.D: Fibrinogen

explanation: Great job! Albumin creates what we call oncotic pressure—think of it as a magnet pulling fluid back into the bloodstream so it doesn't leak out into the tissues. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T14#GNS123_U3_T14_h2)

question: Which common insect breeds like crazy in stagnant floodwaters after heavy rains or a disaster?

options.A: Earthworms
options.B: Mosquitoes
options.C: Butterflies
options.D: Honeybees

explanation: Still floodwaters are breeding paradises for mosquitoes, driving up malaria risks. Netting and draining standing water are key nursing interventions! [learn more](GNS315_U5_T5#GNS315_U5_T5_h7)

question: When patients engage in emotional eating, what is usually driving the habit?

options.A: Stress, boredom, or anxiety
options.B: Lack of clean drinking water
options.C: High environmental temperatures
options.D: Low physical activity levels

explanation: Correct! Many people reach for snacks not because they are genuinely hungry, but to comfort themselves when feeling stressed, anxious, or bored. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T003#GNS227_U7_T003_h5)

question: What is the minimum number of deliveries required to classify a woman as a grand multipara?

options.A: Three or more deliveries
options.B: Five or more deliveries
options.C: Ten or more deliveries
options.D: Seven or more deliveries

explanation: A grand multipara is clinically defined as a woman who has completed five or more pregnancies resulting in live or stillborn infants at or beyond twenty weeks of gestation. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T008#GNS226_U4_T008_h1)

question: Why do we say a resident's care plan must be treated as a living document?

options.A: It is legally required to be rewritten word-for-word every single morning.
options.B: It is only used during the initial admission interview and never again.
options.C: It must be adjusted whenever the resident's clinical condition changes.
options.D: It prevents nurses from having to document daily shift assessments.

explanation: A resident's health changes day by day, so their care plan needs to grow and update right along with them. Spot on! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h5)

question: Why does using unsterile instruments during an abortion often lead to severe sepsis?

options.A: The cervix permanently closes and traps natural bodily fluids
options.B: Bacteria are introduced directly into the sterile uterine cavity
options.C: Incomplete emptying of the uterus causes immediate kidney failure
options.D: The body reacts to the metal by producing toxic white blood cells

explanation: Exactly! Unclean tools carry harmful germs straight into the pelvis, which quickly turns into a dangerous, widespread infection. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T004#GNS226_U5_T004_h3)

question: Why are older adults much more prone to bad drug interactions?

options.A: They experience reduced kidney and liver function along with polypharmacy
options.B: They routinely consume excessive amounts of herbal supplements
options.C: Their plasma protein levels are always abnormally elevated
options.D: Their digestive tracts absorb oral medications much faster than younger adults

explanation: As we age, our kidneys and livers don't clear drugs as quickly as they used to. Combine that with taking several medications at once, and drugs can easily build up to harmful levels. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T4#GNS215_U2_T4_h5)

question: How do modern apology laws treat expressions of sympathy from healthcare providers?

options.A: They remove all licensing requirements for doctors involved in adverse events
options.B: They force the hospital to pay double compensation in every civil lawsuit
options.C: They protect humanitarian expressions of sorrow from being used as evidence of fault
options.D: They make it illegal for any nurse to speak directly to a patient's family

explanation: Apology protection laws encourage honesty by making sure that showing human empathy and sorrow cannot be used in court as proof of guilt. [learn more](GST319_U6_T3#GST319_U6_T3_h5)

question: Which barrier method gives the most reliable protection against sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Contraceptive sponges
options.B: Cervical caps
options.C: Diaphragms
options.D: Condoms

explanation: You got it! Condoms create a physical shield over the genitalia, blocking both infectious fluids and skin contact. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T016#GNS226_U6_T016_h5)

question: Why should community midwives collaborate with traditional birth attendants instead of ignoring them?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants outnumber all trained doctors in cities.
options.B: TBAs are often trusted first-line care providers in rural areas.
options.C: TBAs have advanced surgical degrees from university hospitals.
options.D: Government policy requires TBAs to manage major surgical operations.

explanation: Because many women naturally seek out TBAs first, working with them helps redirect high-risk cases to formal health facilities much faster. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T14#GNS225_U3_T14_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of an engineering control in the workplace?

options.A: To punish staff who fail to follow safety instructions
options.B: To provide extra clothing to shield the skin from harm
options.C: To force workers to change their daily habits and routines
options.D: To place a physical barrier between the worker and the hazard

explanation: Engineering controls use physical changes to the environment or equipment to keep workers safe without needing constant human oversight. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: What is the main function of a State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA)?

options.A: To serve as the primary responder for emergencies within the state
options.B: To oversee international trade agreements with neighboring countries
options.C: To manage private commercial banks operating in local communities
options.D: To replace the federal government in running all national elections

question: Why is a skin puncture considered a critical moment for infection control?

question: Why do special children typically require care that goes beyond routine pediatric visits?

question: Which nursing action is a must when managing a timed suppression test?

question: Why do community nurses treat the girl child as a distinct vulnerable group?

question: Where do isolation precautions mostly try to break the chain of infection?

question: Which of these is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC)?

question: Which part of the nervous system tells the bladder to contract so you can pee?

question: Why is there fluid between the thin membranes that wrap around our organs?

question: Why is it crucial to give quick feedback to staff after they submit an incident report?

question: Why do researchers measure participants before and after giving an intervention?

question: Why do we as nursing students need to look back at the history of nutrition?

question: What happens in the body during the resistance stage of stress?

options.C: The body attempts to adapt and cope with the ongoing stressor
options.D: No hormonal or physiological changes take place

question: How often should an emergency nurse reassess an unstable patient?

question: A high-pressure ventilator alarm starts going off. What is the most common culprit?

options.C: A loose connection somewhere in the plastic tubing

question: What does the term 'essential drugs' refer to in Primary Health Care?

question: A patient with Lassa fever spent 10 minutes talking face-to-face with a colleague inside a small office without a mask. How should we view this colleague?

question: Why must a nurse review a client's medical history before recommending a hormonal contraceptive?

question: Which issue is most commonly linked to pelvic floor muscles that are too tight?

options.B: Complete absence of sensation

options.D: Total bladder paralysis

question: Which organs take the biggest hit from long-term iron overload caused by frequent blood transfusions?

options.C: Liver, heart, and endocrine glands

question: What does a public health nurse focus on most during community outreach?

options.C: Installing borehole water pumps for the village
options.D: Prescribing chemotherapy for advanced cancer patients

question: What does the acronym ISBAR stand for in emergency handover communication?

options.A: Investigation, Symptoms, Bleeding, Airway, Respiration

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention programs in substance abuse control?

options.A: Stopping individuals from ever experimenting with harmful drugs in the first place

options.C: Imposing strict criminal prison sentences on local drug traffickers
options.D: Providing immediate emergency detox in a specialized intensive care unit

question: What is the main sign of acute urinary retention?

question: Which of these is a bad practice when choosing a nutritional supplement?

question: Why are active listening and a non-judgmental attitude so important during post-abortion counseling?

question: What is the primary purpose of the countercurrent multiplier system in the kidney medulla?

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient after inserting a retention suppository?

question: Where do Clostridium tetani spores normally live before getting into the body?

question: Why does community health nursing go beyond just giving care at the bedside?

question: Why can relying only on 'the way we've always done it' (clinical tradition) be tricky in healthcare?

question: What does the term 'artifact' mean on a cardiac monitor?

question: What is your main nursing goal when caring for a patient who just suffered an animal bite or insect sting?

question: Where would you find the exact technical steps for managing a sterile surgical tray in the operating room?

question: Why does a skin pinch test help nurses check a patient's hydration level?

question: Why is it often so hard to enforce anti-FGM laws at the local community level?

question: Why is it so important for the local community to actively take part in health programs?

question: Why is keeping patients in prolonged physical restraints at some spiritual healing camps a major concern?

question: If a ward suddenly admits many new patients and uses up way more syringes and IV fluids, how are these supplies classed?

question: Why is a previous cesarean section considered a contraindication for home delivery?

question: What is the main goal of deep brain stimulation (DBS) for Parkinson's disease?

options.D: To replace damaged cerebrospinal fluid with synthetic dopamine

explanation: DBS uses tiny implanted wires to send gentle electrical pulses, acting like a pacemaker for the brain to block the faulty signals causing tremors and stiffness. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T4#GNS222_U4_T4_h5)

question: A hospital safety committee has limited funds and must fix hazards. Which risk should they tackle first?

options.A: A frequent risk that can cause permanent patient disability
options.B: A rare risk that causes a minor inconvenience to visitors
options.C: A paperwork delay that does not affect direct patient care
options.D: A one-time complaint about the taste of the drinking water

explanation: Risks with high frequency and severe consequences demand immediate action to prevent serious patient harm. [learn more](GST319_U4_T6#GST319_U4_T6_h3)

question: In which of these situations would passing an NG tube through the nose be a huge NO-GO (contraindication)?

options.A: History of controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus
options.B: Localized skin infection on the lower leg
options.C: Mild chronic hypertension managed with medication
options.D: Severe facial trauma with a suspected skull fracture

explanation: Spotting a skull fracture means you never want to push anything through the nose—otherwise, the tube could accidentally find its way into the brain! Safety first. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T1#GNS212_U1_T1_h2)

question: How does acute physical or emotional stress falsely affect a Glucose Tolerance Test?

options.A: It destroys red blood cells and ruins the laboratory blood samples
options.B: It releases hormones like adrenaline and cortisol that raise blood sugar
options.C: It slows down digestion so the stomach cannot absorb the glucose drink
options.D: It forces the pancreas to release too much insulin, causing severe hypoglycemia

explanation: Stress hormones mobilize stored energy and push blood glucose levels up, which can mimic diabetes during the test. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h6)

question: What do collagen fibers mainly give to our bones?

options.A: Electrical impulse conduction
options.B: Absolute rigidity and hardness
options.C: Tensile strength and flexibility
options.D: Direct blood supply and oxygen

explanation: Collagen is like the tough rubber bands inside bone—it gives flexibility so they bend slightly instead of shattering like glass. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T4#GNS121_U3_T4_h2)

question: What do the three classic signs of diabetes—polyuria, polydipsia, and polyphagia—actually mean?

options.A: Frequent headaches, blurred vision, and dizziness
options.B: High blood pressure, rapid heart rate, and fever
options.C: Joint pain, muscle weakness, and skin rashes
options.D: Excessive urination, excessive thirst, and excessive hunger

explanation: Just break down the medical terms: 'uria' relates to urine, 'dipsia' to thirst, and 'phagia' to eating/hunger! Remembering the Greek roots makes nursing terms so much easier. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the very first action a nurse should take when a patient shows signs of severe drug toxicity?

options.A: Stop the administration of the offending medication
options.B: Increase the intravenous fluid rate without a doctor's order
options.C: Document the event in the patient's chart at the end of the shift
options.D: Ask the patient to walk around the room to stay awake

explanation: Stopping the drug source prevents any more of the toxic substance from entering the patient's system. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T2#GNS215_U5_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is included in a comprehensive nutrition history?

options.A: Family tree and genetic ancestry
options.B: Medical history and medication use
options.C: Recent travel history outside the country
options.D: Workplace safety hazard inspections

explanation: Medical conditions and medications heavily influence how the body absorbs and uses nutrients, making them essential parts of a nutrition history. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T002#GNS227_U5_T002_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of translational research in nursing?

options.A: To move lab discoveries into actual bedside patient care
options.B: To change hospital policies without any scientific proof
options.C: To translate foreign medical books into local languages
options.D: To convert qualitative interviews into numerical charts

explanation: You're doing great! Translational research helps bridge the gap between science discoveries in a lab and everyday clinical practice so patients benefit faster. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T4#GNS217_U1_T4_h6)

question: Why do nurses need to care about the food myths our patients believe?

options.A: Myths directly shape daily eating habits and health choices
options.B: Nurses are required to rewrite local recipe books
options.C: Patients will refuse all medications if they have food myths
options.D: Myths are always illegal to follow in a hospital setting

explanation: What people believe dictates what they put on their plates. Understanding this helps us guide patients better without making them feel judged! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T017#GNS227_U2_T017_h1)

question: Where does home quarantine take place?

options.A: At the airport arrival lounge
options.B: Inside a specialized infectious disease hospital ward
options.C: In a government-run military camp
options.D: At the individual's private residence

explanation: Home quarantine allows exposed persons to remain in their own homes while restricting outside visitors and public outings. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h3)

question: As a community health nurse, what is one of your key responsibilities regarding social services?

options.A: Drafting new national legislation for disability rights in parliament
options.B: Connecting patients and families with appropriate community resources and referrals
options.C: Managing government financial budgets for social welfare departments
options.D: Constructing physical ramps and elevators in public buildings

explanation: Nurses act as wonderful bridge-builders! You spot patient needs and point them toward the correct social support agencies. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T16#GNS225_U5_T16_h7)

question: Why do many teenage girls experience irregular periods shortly after starting menstruation?

options.A: Poor nutrition always disrupts adolescent cycles
options.B: The brain-to-ovary hormone pathway is still maturing
options.C: They lack sufficient body fat for hormones
options.D: Endometrial tissue is not fully formed yet

explanation: Just like learning to ride a bicycle, the brain and ovaries take a couple of years to sync up their chemical communication after a girl's first period. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h4)

question: Why must a nurse know the exact landmarks of the vulva?

options.A: To pass a urinary catheter without missing the urethra
options.B: To prevent ovarian cysts
options.C: To measure blood pressure correctly
options.D: To track the exact day of ovulation

explanation: Spot on! Knowing your anatomy keeps procedures safe and stops you from accidentally placing a catheter into the vaginal opening instead of the urethra. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T2#GNS311_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT one of the core elements of Post-Abortion Care?

options.A: Contraceptive and family planning services
options.B: Treatment of abortion-related medical complications
options.C: Counseling for emotional and reproductive needs
options.D: Routine major abdominal surgery for all patients

explanation: Spot on! Routine major surgery is not part of PAC. Complications are usually managed with minor procedures like MVA or medical treatment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h2)

question: A student nurse uses her password to log into the EMR and opens the chart of a famous musician on another floor just out of curiosity. What has happened here?

options.A: A helpful act of teamwork to see if the patient needs extra visitors
options.B: A routine computer system update performed by the IT department
options.C: An unauthorized privacy breach that can be tracked by audit software
options.D: Standard nursing practice for checking hospital bed occupancy rates

explanation: Patient privacy is sacred! Opening a chart without a direct clinical reason breaks confidentiality rules and will be flagged by the system. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T9#GNS212_U4_T9_h5)

question: A pregnant woman at 12 weeks has long-term high blood pressure and is carrying twins. What should you, as her nurse, watch out for?

options.A: She has zero risk of complications because she is young.
options.B: She should stop all her blood pressure tablets right away.
options.C: She only needs normal, routine antenatal visits.
options.D: She needs closer monitoring for early signs of preeclampsia.

explanation: Having twins plus chronic high blood pressure puts her at a higher risk, so we need to keep a closer, caring eye on her throughout her pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h3)

question: Why should you tell your patient NOT to bend their elbow right after getting blood drawn?

options.A: It forces the needle site to bleed faster than normal
options.B: It increases the risk of bruising and hematoma formation
options.C: It stops the remaining blood from flowing into the fingers
options.D: It causes the adhesive bandage to fall off the arm

explanation: Bending the arm puts pressure on the fresh puncture spot, which pops the clot loose and causes blood to leak underneath the skin into a nasty bruise. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h8)

question: In the '5 As' smoking cessation framework, which step means checking if a patient uses tobacco during every clinic visit?

options.A: Assess
options.B: Advise
options.C: Ask
options.D: Arrange

explanation: The 'Ask' step is simply checking and recording whether every patient uses tobacco. Simple, direct, and essential for good nursing care! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T5#GNS313_U3_T5_h5)

question: The main reason a patient with high blood pressure might stop taking their medication is that...

options.A: blood pressure pills must only be taken for one week
options.B: the condition usually causes no daily physical symptoms
options.C: pharmacies always keep drug prices extremely low
options.D: hypertension disappears completely without treatment

explanation: Because high blood pressure is often a silent killer, patients feel fine and mistakenly assume they do not need their daily pills. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T5#GNS215_U4_T5_h2)

question: What exactly is an 'out-of-pocket' payment in healthcare?

options.A: A monthly tax deducted automatically from a civil servant's salary
options.B: Direct cash paid by a patient to a provider at the time of service
options.C: Financial aid given by foreign countries to build clinics
options.D: A reimbursement paid by an insurance company to a hospital

explanation: An out-of-pocket payment is cash you bring straight from your purse or pocket to pay the hospital cash-and-carry style right when you get treated. [learn more](GST322_U4_T1#GST322_U4_T1_h2)

question: What does 'data saturation' mean during qualitative interviews?

options.A: All participants have completed their medical treatments
options.B: The researcher has run out of financial funding for the study
options.C: The audio recording devices have stopped working properly
options.D: No new information or themes are emerging from interviews

explanation: Think of a sponge that is fully soaked. Saturation means you've heard it all; conducting more interviews isn't bringing up anything new, so you can wrap up! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h4)

question: A patient with severe preeclampsia suddenly stops passing urine and shows signs of fluid overload. What should you do first as the nurse?

options.A: Encourage her to drink large volumes of oral water to flush the kidneys
options.B: Administer oral diuretics without a doctor's order to force urination
options.C: Monitor for respiratory distress and report failing urine output immediately
options.D: Prepare the patient for immediate home discharge with dietary advice

explanation: Not peeing plus fluid overload is an urgent red flag! Fluid can back up into the lungs, so reporting this immediately can save a life. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T007#GNS226_U4_T007_h6)

question: A nurse sees imported vaccines with broken safety seals. Which agency should be alerted immediately?

options.A: The Nigerian Police Force
options.B: National Bureau of Statistics
options.C: NAFDAC
options.D: NMCN

explanation: Great thinking! NAFDAC is our national watchdog for checking the safety and quality of drugs, vaccines, and medical products coming into the country. [learn more](GST321_U10_T2#GST321_U10_T2_h2)

question: Why do hospital cleaners and nurses wipe down bed rails and bedside tables so often?

options.A: Air currents deposit airborne droplets directly onto these objects
options.B: Patients spend most of their recovery time touching these areas
options.C: Microorganisms multiply rapidly on metal surfaces without moisture
options.D: These surfaces act as common fomites for indirect contact spread

explanation: Exactly! High-touch areas easily collect germs from hands and pass them along to the next person, which is why cleaning them stops indirect spread. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to help a patient with a poor appetite?

options.A: Offering small, frequent nutrient-dense snacks
options.B: Enhancing flavors with herbs and spices
options.C: Using adaptive eating devices like scooped plates
options.D: Forcing the patient to eat large meals quickly before they get tired

explanation: Rushing or forcing food only adds stress and wears the patient out, making them eat even less. Patience and gentle encouragement work best! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h6)

question: A mother believes her child's fever is caused by witchcraft rather than malaria, and avoids the clinic. What is the best way for a nurse to respond?

options.A: Respectfully listen to her concerns while gently explaining malaria transmission and treatment
options.B: Scold the mother for holding backward beliefs that put her child in mortal danger
options.C: Call the local security forces to force the mother to accept malaria medication
options.D: Ignore her cultural beliefs and quietly administer the drugs without telling her

explanation: Good nursing means meeting patients where they are. Building trust and respecting cultural concerns helps us guide patients toward safe, proven treatments. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T7#GNS313_U2_T7_h7)

question: What usually happens when a hospital's stated values do not match how its leaders actually behave?

options.A: Trust dissolves rapidly among staff and stakeholders
options.B: The organization immediately goes bankrupt by law
options.C: State licensing boards automatically lower facility taxes
options.D: Employees begin working harder to compensate for leaders

explanation: When leaders say one thing and do another, hypocrisy kills workplace trust and staff morale very quickly. [learn more](GST321_U1_T1#GST321_U1_T1_h4)

question: What happens if a nurse chooses a stockinette that is too narrow for a patient's leg?

options.A: It will dissolve when the plaster gets wet
options.B: It can squeeze the limb and restrict blood circulation
options.C: It will automatically stretch to fit any size perfectly
options.D: It will fall off the leg before the cast is applied

explanation: An undersized stockinette acts like a tourniquet when stretched tightly over a limb, cutting off proper blood flow. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h4)

question: A newly graduated nurse is left completely alone on a specialized ward with no supervision. Which leadership style does this reflect, and what is the likely result?

options.A: Transactional; it will ensure all bonuses are paid correctly
options.B: Autocratic; it will improve immediate staff teamwork
options.C: Laissez-faire; it may cause anxiety and compromise patient safety
options.D: Democratic; it will encourage healthy group discussions

explanation: New nurses need support and supervision, so a hands-off approach often leads to distress and unsafe patient care. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the main goal of primary health care (PHC) services in Nigeria?

options.A: Handling complex surgical procedures for urban residents
options.B: Conducting advanced medical research in laboratories
options.C: Training international medical specialists
options.D: Bringing essential health services close to the grassroots

explanation: You've got this! Primary health care is all about bringing basic, friendly health services right down to the local communities where everyday people live. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T5#GNS124_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why do facial stitches need to be removed much sooner than stitches on a knee or back?

options.A: Facial skin is much thicker than skin on the back
options.B: The face heals faster due to a rich blood supply
options.C: Stitches on the face cause less scarring if left longer
options.D: Facial muscles do not move during daily activities

explanation: The abundant blood supply in the head and neck allows rapid healing, requiring early suture removal to prevent track marks. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which temporary foetal structure turns into the ligamentum arteriosum after birth?

options.A: Umbilical vein
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Ductus arteriosus
options.D: Foramen ovale

explanation: Spot on! Once the ductus arteriosus finishes its job and seals up with high oxygen levels, it turns into a sturdy little ligament called the ligamentum arteriosum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T006#GNS226_U2_T006_h7)

question: A heart failure patient reports a sudden weight gain over two days during a tele-nursing call. What does this likely mean?

options.A: A healthy improvement in overall nutritional status
options.B: Normal muscle growth from starting a new exercise plan
options.C: Fluid retention that needs prompt medical evaluation
options.D: A broken weighing scale with no clinical relevance

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Rapid weight gain in heart failure usually points to dangerous fluid build-up that needs quick attention. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h6)

question: What does the Phosphatase Test check for during milk processing?

options.A: The exact percentage of fat and protein present
options.B: The total number of live bacteria in the sample
options.C: Whether pasteurization was successfully carried out
options.D: If antibiotics were given to the dairy cattle

explanation: You got it! The enzyme alkaline phosphatase is naturally killed off by proper heating. If the test shows the enzyme is gone, it proves the milk was successfully pasteurized. [learn more](GST114_U5_T5#GST114_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why do STI infections in the male urethra often lead to swelling and pus?

options.A: The body produces extra oil to protect the skin from dryness
options.B: White blood cells rush to the invasion site to fight the microbes
options.C: Urine mixes with blood cells to create a protective barrier
options.D: Microbes block normal urine flow and cause back pressure

explanation: Think of white blood cells as your body's emergency responders. When germs attack, they flood the area to fight back, creating that pus we see in infections. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h3)

question: Which symptom helps tell a yeast infection apart from trichomoniasis?

options.A: A painless firm chancre on the external labia
options.B: Frothy, yellow-green discharge with a strong, fishy smell
options.C: Painful, fluid-filled vesicles that rupture into open ulcers
options.D: Thick, white, cottage-cheese-like discharge with no foul odor

explanation: Yeast infections (candidiasis) usually bring thick, white discharge and intense itching, unlike the frothy, foul-smelling discharge of trichomoniasis. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h5)

question: A nursing mother says her milk suddenly stops flowing when she gets stressed or anxious in a crowded room. Why does this happen?

options.A: Stress inhibits the release of oxytocin, preventing the let-down reflex.
options.B: High adrenaline levels directly destroy colostrum inside the lactiferous ducts.
options.C: Anxiety causes prolactin receptors in the alveoli to temporarily close.
options.D: Fear triggers an immediate decrease in the systemic production of estrogen.

explanation: Stress and anxiety release adrenaline, which can block oxytocin. Without oxytocin, the milk doesn't 'let down,' even though it's inside the breast! [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h5)

question: What is the standard lab test used to check for urinary schistosomiasis?

options.A: Blood culture to isolate active bacterial colonies
options.B: Urine microscopy using filtration to find eggs
options.C: Chest X-ray to visualize lung calcifications
options.D: Liver biopsy to inspect adult worm clusters

explanation: By filtering a urine sample, lab technicians can catch the tiny parasite eggs under a microscope. Simple, non-invasive, and effective! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h5)

question: What is the most common cause of heavy bleeding right after childbirth (primary PPH)?

options.A: Retained surgical gauze
options.B: Uterine atony
options.C: Coagulation disorders
options.D: Cervical laceration

explanation: Spot on! Uterine atony happens when the uterine muscles are too tired to clamp down after delivery. Recognizing this helps you save mothers every day! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which fetal structure allows blood to flow directly from the right atrium to the left atrium?

options.A: Foramen ovale
options.B: Ductus venosus
options.C: Umbilical vein
options.D: Ductus arteriosus

explanation: The foramen ovale is an opening between the upper heart chambers that lets blood skip the right ventricle and lungs. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T9#GNS121_U6_T9_h2)

question: What is the minimum recommended interval between pregnancies to protect maternal and child health?

options.A: At least two years
options.B: Exactly six months
options.C: Three to four weeks
options.D: At least five years

explanation: Spacing pregnancies by at least two years gives the mother's body enough time to recover and lowers infant health risks. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h2)

question: What is the protective little wall of cells that the immune system builds around TB bacteria called?

options.A: Abscess
options.B: Hematoma
options.C: Aneurysm
options.D: Granuloma

explanation: Your immune system tries to trap the germs by building a wall of cells around them. This little cluster is called a granuloma or tubercle. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is it important to report research findings back to the community where a study took place?

options.A: It prevents community members from asking questions about the budget
options.B: It ensures the researchers receive financial bonuses from donors
options.C: It is required by law before any doctor can write a prescription
options.D: It builds mutual trust and respects the participants who gave their time

explanation: Returning results to the community honors participants and fosters cooperative relationships for future health projects. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T2#GNS224_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main job of early defibrillation in the Chain of Survival?

options.A: It prevents blood clots from forming inside the coronary arteries
options.B: It corrects abnormal heart rhythms like ventricular fibrillation
options.C: It inflates the lungs with high concentrations of oxygen
options.D: It restarts a completely stopped flatline heart

explanation: An AED gives a quick electric shock that resets chaotic heart waves so the heart can settle back into a normal beat. Pretty cool science, right? [learn more](GNS321_U2_T7#GNS321_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which activity is a classic example of primary prevention?

options.A: Giving routine childhood immunizations
options.B: Treating complications of advanced diabetes
options.C: Performing a blood pressure screening clinic
options.D: Providing physical therapy after a stroke

explanation: Vaccines protect healthy people from contracting a specific disease in the first place, which defines primary prevention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h2)

question: A community health nurse is planning a schistosomiasis prevention program in a rural Nigerian village. Which action will provide the most lasting protection?

options.A: Installing clean, accessible piped water and functional sanitation toilets
options.B: Providing free malaria mosquito nets to every household in the village
options.C: Instructing villagers to boil all river water before using it for cooking
options.D: Giving nutritional supplements to adults to boost their body weight

explanation: Clean tap water and proper toilets mean villagers won't need to step into infected streams or contaminate the water sources. That's how we solve the root cause! You're thinking like a true nurse. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T10#GNS214_U1_T10_h8)

question: Why is boosting domestic revenue (like local taxes and insurance) so important for a sustainable healthcare system?

options.A: It reduces heavy reliance on unpredictable foreign donor funds and loans
options.B: It eliminates the need for professional nursing regulatory bodies
options.C: It stops patients from visiting hospitals for routine checkups
options.D: It guarantees that all private clinics become government-owned

explanation: Building internal financial strength gives a country independence, ensuring its health sector stays steady even if foreign grants change. [learn more](GST322_U3_T2#GST322_U3_T2_h7)

question: Which sign is a key indicator of severe dehydration in a young child?

options.A: Bounding peripheral pulses
options.B: Lethargy or unconsciousness
options.C: Excessive tearing and crying
options.D: Eager drinking when offered a cup

explanation: When the body loses too much fluid and blood volume drops, the brain suffers, making the child very drowsy, limp, or unresponsive. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T18#GNS215_U6_T18_h5)

question: What is the main job of the ovaries in the female body?

options.A: Storing urine before it reaches the bladder
options.B: Producing eggs and female hormones
options.C: Filtering waste from the lower abdomen
options.D: Producing red blood cells during pregnancy

explanation: You got this! The ovaries are our female reproductive glands that make ova (eggs) and important hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h1)

question: What is the main job of psychological defense mechanisms?

options.A: To permanently cure chronic depression
options.B: To improve physical muscle strength under stress
options.C: To shield the mind from sudden emotional pain and anxiety
options.D: To increase conscious awareness of personal faults

explanation: Think of defense mechanisms as a mental shock absorber. They protect us unconsciously when stress or bad news feels too heavy to process all at once. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the correct way to apply a new transdermal medication patch?

options.A: Remove the old patch and clean the skin before placing the new one on a different site
options.B: Use bare fingers to rub the sticky side firmly onto hairy skin areas
options.C: Cut the patch in half if the prescribed dose is too strong for the patient
options.D: Put the new patch directly on top of the old one to keep the medication level high

explanation: Always take off the old patch first and pick a fresh skin site! Rotating spots prevents skin irritation, and removing the old one prevents accidental overdoses. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T5#GNS125_U4_T5_h5)

question: Why is it important to clearly define the scope of a community health assessment?

options.A: It shortens the nursing shift schedule for the week
options.B: It eliminates the need to talk to community members
options.C: It guarantees that zero diseases will occur in the area
options.D: It keeps the assessment focused on specific health problems

explanation: Communities have many needs, but trying to fix everything at once can overwhelm your team. Setting a clear scope helps you stay focused and realistic! [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is the primary shape of human kidneys?

options.A: Bean-shaped
options.B: Disc-shaped
options.C: Spherical
options.D: Crescent-shaped

explanation: Human kidneys have a characteristic bean shape and sit in the posterior abdominal wall. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h1)

question: A newborn baby experiences a sudden drop in blood oxygen levels shortly after delivery. Which foetal shunt is most likely to remain open or reopen due to this stress?

options.A: The ductus arteriosus
options.B: The umbilical vein
options.C: The ductus venosus
options.D: The portal sinus

explanation: Low oxygen levels and respiratory distress in a newborn can keep the muscular ductus arteriosus open or cause it to dilate. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T8#GNS121_U6_T8_h6)

question: A patient experiencing severe shortness of breath is unlikely to focus on which type of need at that moment?

options.A: Getting enough oxygen into the lungs
options.B: Achieving personal growth and self-actualization
options.C: Maintaining basic fluid balance
options.D: Relieving physical pain

explanation: Until basic physiological survival needs like breathing are met, higher-level needs such as self-actualization take a back seat. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: Where should you file an incident report after a medication mishap?

options.A: In the hospital's internal quality improvement system
options.B: In the public national medical registry
options.C: In the patient's permanent clinical medical record
options.D: In the personal nursing license file

explanation: Correct! Incident reports go into the hospital's internal quality system to help us learn and improve—they don't go into the patient's official clinical chart. [learn more](GST319_U5_T1#GST319_U5_T1_h6)

question: How does nurse involvement in community support networks benefit the broader health system?

options.A: It empowers volunteers and lightens the workload on formal clinic staff
options.B: It restricts patient interactions strictly inside the hospital building
options.C: It ensures that nurses make all decisions without community input
options.D: It eliminates the need for any medications in chronic disease care

explanation: By training community members to help run support networks, health centers extend their reach and ease pressure on busy clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h6)

question: How does teaching lifestyle habits help a patient with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: It cures the genetic condition entirely through proper daily nutrition and rest
options.B: It guarantees that they will never experience chronic fatigue or joint pain again
options.C: It teaches them how to safely perform their own blood transfusions at home
options.D: It helps them avoid common triggers like dehydration and extreme cold to prevent crises

explanation: Knowledge is power! When patients know what sets off a crisis—like staying hydrated or dressing warmly—they can take charge of their daily health and stay out of the hospital. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h8)

question: How does heavy domestic labor mostly harm a young girl's development?

options.A: It robs her of time needed for education, rest, and personal growth.
options.B: It improves her cardiovascular endurance permanently.
options.C: It automatically grants her legal emancipation from her parents.
options.D: It prevents her from ever contracting vector-borne diseases.

explanation: When chores take over, kids miss out on school and the simple rest they need to grow up healthy and strong. Every child deserves time to just be a child! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T5#GNS225_U5_T5_h2)

question: What happens to joint structures over many years if metabolic joint disease is left completely untreated?

options.A: Complete regeneration of healthy joint tissue and natural healing
options.B: Softening of the bones until they become completely flexible
options.C: Permanent bone erosion, cartilage destruction, and severe deformity
options.D: Total fusion of the skin directly to the underlying muscle tissue

explanation: Without treatment, ongoing inflammation and tophi will gradually wear down the bone and cartilage, leading to permanent joint damage. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h9)

question: Why do joint sprains (injured ligaments) usually take a really long time to heal?

options.A: Muscles pull the torn ends apart constantly
options.B: Synovial fluid continuously dissolves new scar tissue
options.C: Fibrocartilage replaces all normal collagen
options.D: Ligaments have a poor blood supply

explanation: Brilliant insight! Ligaments don't have many blood vessels running through them, meaning they receive less oxygen and nutrients, so repair takes time. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T6#GNS121_U3_T6_h8)

question: What is the basic building block of all living human structures?

options.A: Organs
options.B: Cells
options.C: Tissues
options.D: Systems

explanation: Cells are recognized universally as the fundamental units of structure and function in the human body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T9#GNS111_U1_T9_h1)

question: What underlying condition is the most frequent cause of oesophageal varices (enlarged veins)?

options.A: Portal hypertension from liver cirrhosis
options.B: Chronic bacterial infection of the stomach
options.C: Enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck
options.D: Severe long-term dietary iron deficiency

explanation: When the liver is scarred (cirrhosis), blood can't flow through it easily. This backs up pressure into nearby vessels, including the fragile veins in the oesophagus. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T5#GNS213_U3_T5_h5)

question: What symptom turns pre-eclampsia into full-blown eclampsia?

options.A: Total cessation of fetal heart tones
options.B: A sudden drop in body temperature
options.C: The onset of convulsive seizures
options.D: Severe localized pain in the lower back

explanation: Spot on! Pre-eclampsia has high blood pressure and protein in the urine, but once seizures start, it is classified as eclampsia. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T009#GNS226_U1_T009_h3)

question: Why can cultural beliefs and stigma create obstacles during problem identification?

options.A: Stigma forces communities to build private hospitals for themselves
options.B: Local customs automatically cure all infectious diseases without treatment
options.C: Residents may hide health issues or distrust outside health workers
options.D: Traditional rulers refuse to let nurses keep written records

explanation: Fear of stigma and lack of trust in outsiders can prevent community members from sharing true health problems. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h8)

question: During the early (compensated) stage of shock, why do the skin and limbs often feel cool and pale?

options.A: Red blood cells lose their oxygen-carrying capacity in peripheral tissues
options.B: The ambient room temperature directly lowers the peripheral skin temperature
options.C: Blood is shunted away from non-vital areas to protect the heart and brain
options.D: Superficial blood vessels dilate to release excess heat from the body core

explanation: Think of the body as a smart manager: when resources are low, it redirects blood away from the skin and tummy to keep vital organs like the heart and brain happy. That's why the hands and feet get cool and pale first! [learn more](GNS112_U7_T3#GNS112_U7_T3_h2)

question: What makes intravenous therapy risky regarding how fast drugs act?

options.B: Unpredictable absorption from the gut
options.C: Total immunity to local tissue irritation
options.D: The rapid irreversibility of drug action

explanation: You're doing great! Once a medicine goes straight into the vein, you cannot take it back out. That's why we always double-check our doses—reactions happen fast and are harder to reverse than oral pills. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T5#GNS125_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary aim of culturally sensitive nutrition counseling in nursing?

options.A: Forcing patients to abandon their cultural heritage completely
options.B: Convincing doctors to change hospital meal timetables
options.C: Replacing all local dishes with imported western food items
options.D: Finding acceptable local food substitutes that maintain good nutrition

explanation: We don't need to fight a patient's culture! Instead, we work with what they have, suggesting safe, affordable local foods that provide the exact same nutrients. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h7)

question: During a postpartum breast check, which sign strongly suggests the baby is not latching on correctly?

options.A: Prominent superficial veins
options.B: Bilateral breast symmetry
options.C: Cracked or bleeding nipples
options.D: Palpable lactiferous sinuses

explanation: A good latch should only feel like a gentle tug. If the mother's nipples are cracked, sore, or bleeding, it's a classic red flag that the baby is latching onto the nipple instead of taking enough of the areola. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T10#GNS121_U7_T10_h8)
